skill.name: am-i-drifting
skill.description: Compare how someone writes now against how they used to write, and name what has changed. Use when someone asks whether they still sound like themselves, whether their posts have got worse or blander, whether AI has flattened their writing, or wants their recent posts compared with their older ones. Do not use it to compare one person against another person.
skill.summary: Compare older and recent posts from the same writer to identify specific voice changes and suggest up to three habits to restore.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Identify Changes in Your Writing Voice
content.value_statement: Recent posts can lose familiar writing habits without making the changes obvious. This skill compares your past and present writing and recommends concrete habits to restore.
actual_capabilities: Compare five older posts and five recent posts from the same writer.
Describe each period separately through openings, sentence length, vocabulary, personal detail, and structure.
Identify specific changes such as hedging, abstraction, increasing length, borrowed phrasing, and reduced individuality.
Ask about deliberate audience or register changes before treating differences as deterioration.
Recommend at most three concrete writing habits without inventing a numerical score from small samples.
When VoiceMOAT is connected, use voice insights, posts, and analytics to contextualize changes, with scored Voice Guard drift available on Twitter.
limitations: Without older samples, the workflow can describe current writing but cannot establish changes over time.
The workflow compares one writer with their own history, not different writers, and does not prove AI caused a change.
VoiceMOAT tools require a connected Pro or Enterprise account; voice analysis requires Voice Lab to have run.
Voice Guard scored drift is Twitter only; LinkedIn provides Voice Lab analysis and posts without that scored comparison.

use_cases.title: Review Personal Posting Habits
use_cases.description: Compare earlier and recent posts to identify lost personal details, changed openings, or increased hedging.

use_cases.title: Assess a Deliberate Audience Change
use_cases.description: Check whether a new professional audience explains a changed register before deciding which familiar habits to restore.

use_cases.title: Support an Evidence-Based Editorial Review
use_cases.description: Review one client against their own earlier writing and offer up to three concrete adjustments supported by sample differences.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Compare My Posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these five older posts with these five recent posts from me. Describe each period, then name specific changes. Older: [posts]. Recent: [posts].
prompt_templates.scenario: A first review using two supplied writing samples.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Check for Less Personal Writing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my older and recent posts for hedging, abstraction, length changes, and fewer personal details. Cite examples without a score. Older: [posts]. Recent: [posts].
prompt_templates.scenario: A focused review of suspected changes in writing voice.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Account for a New Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: My audience changed from [old audience] to [new audience]. Compare my older and recent posts, ask about intent, and recommend at most three habits. Older: [posts]. Recent: [posts].
prompt_templates.scenario: A review that separates deliberate register changes from unwanted drift.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Review Connected Account Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: With my connected VoiceMOAT account, review voice insights, posts, and analytics. Use Voice Guard drift if available on Twitter. Explain unavailable evidence and recommend up to three habits.
prompt_templates.scenario: An account review requiring the connector plan and completed Voice Lab analysis.

output_examples.input: Compare five older posts with personal stories and five recent posts using broad industry claims.
output: Earlier voice: Four of five posts begin with a personal event, followed by a specific lesson.
Recent voice: None begin with personal events; three start with broad industry claims.
Change: Personal openings have been replaced by general statements.
Before recommending changes: Was this shift intended for a different audience?
Possible habit to restore: Begin selected posts with a concrete event you experienced.

output_examples.input: I only have my five latest posts. Can you tell whether my voice has changed?
output_examples.output: I can describe your current writing, but I cannot establish a change without older samples. Please provide earlier posts from a distinct period.

output_examples.input: Can my connected LinkedIn account provide a scored Voice Guard comparison?
output_examples.output: Voice Guard scored drift is Twitter only. LinkedIn can provide Voice Lab analysis and posts, provided Voice Lab has run on the account.

best_practices: Provide five older posts from a period you valued and five recent posts, with a meaningful time gap.
State audience, role, or tone changes that may explain intentional differences.
Request concrete sample evidence and prioritize no more than three habits to restore.
anti_patterns: Comparing different writers instead of one writer against their own past.
Requesting a precise voice score from ten pasted posts or inferring trends without older samples.
Treating every style change as deterioration without checking the intended audience or register.

faq.question: What samples should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide five posts from a period when you valued your writing and five recent posts. Choose periods separated by a meaningful gap.

faq.question: Can this work without older posts?
faq.answer: It can describe your current writing, but it cannot establish what changed without an older comparison set.

faq.question: Will it give my writing a score?
faq.answer: It does not invent scores from pasted samples. A connected Twitter account may provide the separate Voice Guard drift score.

faq.question: Can it prove AI changed my voice?
faq.answer: No. It can identify changes in supplied writing, but those changes do not establish their cause.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. Pasted posts support the basic workflow. Connected analysis requires VoiceMOAT Pro or Enterprise, and voice insights require completed Voice Lab analysis.

faq.question: Does LinkedIn support scored drift analysis?
faq.answer: No. Voice Guard scored drift is Twitter only. LinkedIn supports Voice Lab analysis and posts when the required account analysis is available.
